benchmark_type_evidence: we introduce MATH, a new dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems
brief_description: MATH is a dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems (from AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, etc.) with step-by-step solutions in LaTeX, spanning 7 subjects and 5 difficulty levels. It is accompanied by AMPS, a large auxiliary pretraining corpus of over 5 million mathematics problems from Khan Academy and Mathematica scripts.

datasets.variant_notes: 7 subjects (Prealgebra, Algebra, Number Theory, Counting and Probability, Geometry, Intermediate Algebra, Precalculus) with 5 difficulty levels each
datasets.annotation_method: Problems collected from US mathematics competitions (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, etc.) via aops.com; solutions written in LaTeX with step-by-step derivations

data_creator_info.creator_type: competition organizers (original problems) + paper authors (curation, formatting)
data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: UC Berkeley, UChicago; problems sourced from Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) community
data_creator_info.evidence: problems from mathematics competitions including the AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and more. Many of these problems can be collected from aops.com/community/c3158_usa_contests

datasets.notes: 12,500 problems total (7,500 training, 5,000 test). Problems tagged by difficulty 1-5. Answers normalized for exact-match evaluation using \boxed{} delimiter. Problems and solutions formatted in LaTeX with Asymptote vector graphics language for figures.

datasets.variant_notes: Two subsets: Khan Academy (~100,000 problems) and Mathematica (~5 million problems)
datasets.annotation_method: Khan Academy problems pulled from Khan Academy exercises (github.com/Khan/khan-exercises); Mathematica problems generated from 100 hand-designed scripts (37 with step-by-step solutions)

data_creator_info.creator_type: Khan Academy (existing exercises) + paper authors (Mathematica scripts)
data_creator_info.evidence: Khan Academy subset has 693 exercise types with over 100,000 problems and full solutions... we also contribute our own Mathematica scripts to generate approximately 50x more problems

datasets.notes: 23 GB total. Khan Academy covers elementary math to multivariable calculus. Mathematica covers algebra, calculus, counting, statistics, geometry, linear algebra, number theory. Designed as auxiliary pretraining dataset for MATH.

translated.evidence: Problems sourced from US mathematics competitions (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME) originally written in English, collected from aops.com. Not translated from another language.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: Problems are from US math competitions and solutions are in LaTeX, but the paper does not describe who specifically wrote or verified the step-by-step solutions or whether they are native English speakers.

culturally_grounded.evidence: MATH consists of abstract mathematical competition problems (algebra, geometry, number theory, etc.) that are culture-neutral by nature. The problems assess mathematical reasoning, not cultural knowledge.

MATH.annotation_quality_notes: Problems sourced from established US math competitions with decades of history. Answers are normalized with explicit formatting rules for exact-match evaluation. Human evaluation reported: CS PhD student ~40%, IMO gold medalist ~90%.

translated.evidence: Khan Academy problems pulled from English-language Khan Academy platform; Mathematica problems generated from hand-designed scripts by the authors. Not translated.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: Khan Academy content is professionally created but annotator details not given. Mathematica scripts designed by the paper authors (UC Berkeley/UChicago).

culturally_grounded.evidence: AMPS is a pretraining corpus of algorithmically generated or curated mathematical exercises. Problems are abstract math, not culturally situated.

AMPS.annotation_quality_notes: Khan Academy subset uses exercises from an established educational platform (693 exercise types). Mathematica subset generated from 100 hand-designed scripts covering diverse math topics. Total 23 GB.

datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: Both datasets are originally created in English. MATH problems collected from US math competitions; AMPS generated from Khan Academy and Mathematica scripts. They are English-original, not translated from another language.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: No datasets are translated from English to other languages. The benchmark is English-only.

details.notes: Both MATH and AMPS consist of abstract mathematical problems (algebra, geometry, number theory, etc.) that are culture-neutral. No cultural grounding is attempted or relevant.

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: The paper does not report annotator language background. Problems are sourced from US math competitions and Khan Academy (English-medium), and Mathematica scripts were written by UC Berkeley/UChicago researchers.

annotator_workforce.evidence: The paper does not report demographics, compensation, or ethics review. Authors are from UC Berkeley and UChicago. Problems collected from aops.com and Khan Academy.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark is entirely English-language. All problems, solutions, and formatting (LaTeX, Asymptote) are in English. The benchmark assesses mathematical reasoning in English only and makes no claims about multilingual coverage.

geographic_representation.evidence: MATH problems are from US mathematics competitions (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME). These competitions 'assess the mathematical problem-solving ability of the best young mathematical talent in the United States.' Khan Academy is a US-based educational platform.
